## Purpose and scope

This workflow makes every access change at Kestrel Health Network (KHN) start from a human resources (HR) event, not an email. It covers employees, agency nurses from ClearPath Staffing (V-03) and vendor workers from Meridian Clinical Systems (V-01) and NorthArc Cloud (V-02), on the Identity Directory (A-007) and every system it grants through the role-to-permission matrix (BCN-R2-08), including the Clinical Information System (CIS, A-001).

The Health Information Act (section 60) requires safeguards against unauthorized access; access that outlives a job is that risk. The HR feed carries staff personal information under the Protection of Privacy Act, so it sends only the fields used here.

## Sources of truth and events

| Worker type | Source of truth | End date |
|---|---|---|
| Employee | HR and Payroll System (A-015) | Set by HR at termination |
| Agency | A-015 record created by HR from the ClearPath booking | Required: no end date, no account |
| Vendor | A-015 record created by HR for the Kestrel sponsor | Required, no later than the contract end |

A-015 sends each event to the IT Service Management Platform (A-011), which opens a ticket automatically:

- Joiner: a new worker row with effective_from.
- Mover: a new row with a different job_role, department or site_code; HR closes the old row the day before (one current row per worker, rule DQ-12).
- Leaver: hr_status Terminated, or effective_to reached.
- Leave: hr_status Leave disables the account until return (E-040 shows this working).

## Joiner

1. HR enters the hire at least 5 working days before the start (proposed).
2. Provisioning creates the account in A-007 with the birthright permissions for the job_role. The HR record plus the approved matrix is the approval.
3. The worker enrols in multifactor authentication (MFA) at first sign-in; privileged and vendor accounts stay locked until enrolled.
4. CIS access is released when CIS training is recorded complete.
5. The ticket closes when the worker confirms access works.

## Mover

1. On the effective date A-007 adds the new role's permissions and removes the old role's in the same run.
2. Handover overlap only through the access exception process (BCN-R2-14), at most 5 working days (proposed).
3. The new manager confirms the access within 5 working days (proposed).

Case E-028, Chantal Roy: Unit Clerk (ARH Medicine) to Clinical Analyst (KGH) on 2026-08-17. The old row was never closed, so she kept A-001 view chart, A-006 update bed status and A-008 virtual desktop access. Action: close the old row with effective_to 2026-08-16, remove the three permissions, repeat review AR-006.

## Leaver

1. Trigger: hr_status Terminated or effective_to reached, whichever is first. Agency and vendor accounts end on their end date with or without a termination.
2. Disable the A-007 account at the end of the last working day, end sessions, remove every permission and open exception.
3. Check A-007 and CIS audit logs for activity after the end date. Any such access goes to Priya Raman (E-003), Chief Privacy Officer, for the Health Information Act risk-of-harm test (section 60.1).
4. Delete the disabled account after 90 days (proposed); keep audit logs.

| Worker | End | On 2026-10-01 | Last A-007 sign-in | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-014 Olivia Grant, agency nurse | Contract end 2026-08-31 | Enabled; review AR-003 said Remove on 2026-09-25 | 2026-08-29 14:02 | Disable; agree an end-date feed with ClearPath |
| E-027 Jason Kim, registered nurse | Terminated 2026-08-14 | Enabled | 2026-08-13 19:20 | Disable; HR to find why the event never reached IT |

Neither sign-in is after the end date; the CIS audit-log check must still be done before either case closes.

## Daily reconciliation control

At 06:00 each day (proposed) a job compares current HR rows with enabled A-007 accounts and opens a ticket for:

- an enabled account that is Terminated or past effective_to (missed leaver);
- an agency or vendor row with no effective_to (today E-015);
- more than one current row (E-028);
- a manager_id that does not exist (E-037 points to E-099);
- an account in any system with no HR record (AR-018 found E-045 in the CIS).

## Responsibilities and measures

| Activity | HR (E-018) | Manager | Identity and access team | Service desk (E-005) | Security (E-004) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Record event and dates | A, R | C | I | I | I |
| Provision and remove access | I | I | R | A | C |
| Confirm mover access | I | A, R | C | I | I |
| Post-end activity check | C | I | R | I | A |
| Daily reconciliation | C | I | R | A | I |

R responsible, A accountable, C consulted, I informed.

| Measure | Baseline 2026-10-01 (data) | Target (agreed) |
|---|---|---|
| Missed leavers | 2 (E-014, E-027) | 0 |
| Median days to fulfil an access request | 4.26 | 1 |
| Access requests resolved within 72 hours | 27.3% | 80% |
mistakes: Letting a manager's email trigger provisioning instead of the HR record. You lose the single source of truth, and the leaver step then depends on someone remembering.
Treating a mover as a joiner: adding the new access without removing the old role. That is how E-028 kept Unit Clerk access to the CIS and the Bed Management System.
Disabling agency and vendor accounts only when HR processes a termination. Their contracts end without one, which is how E-014 stayed enabled after 2026-08-31.
Closing a leaver case without checking activity after the end date, so a possible privacy breach is never assessed.

## Scope and design principles

This process covers access the joiner-mover-leaver (JML) workflow (BCN-R2-06) does not grant automatically from human resources (HR) events: permissions outside a role, temporary access, vendor sessions and urgent clinical requests. Principles:

- The approved role-to-permission matrix (BCN-R2-08) is the approval for role access.
- The approver is accountable for the system. Requester, approver and provisioner are three different people.
- Every step is timed from IT Service Management Platform (A-011) timestamps.
- Least privilege, and an end date on anything temporary.

## Baseline: where today's process fails

| Measure | Value |

Control failures: Kevin Park (E-009) granted 107 of 171 permission rows (62.6%), two of them to himself, and review AR-003 decided Remove with no action. The portal is the slowest route today, so moving staff to it only helps once the form and approvals are fixed.

## Request routes

| Route | Use for | How | Approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| Role access | Start or move | HR event, automatic | None extra: the matrix |
| Additional permission | Access outside the role | Portal form | System business owner or named delegate |
| Temporary or exception | Time-bound access outside policy | Portal form plus exception record (BCN-R2-14) | Business owner as risk owner; security advises |
| Vendor session | Remote support by V-01 or V-02 | Portal, raised by the Kestrel sponsor | Business owner, per session |
| Urgent clinical | Needed for a shift today | Phone to the service desk, logged at priority 3 (P3) | On-call unit manager; owner confirms next business day |

## Future-state steps and controls

1. Request: the portal form requires employee ID, system, permission, dates and reason. Control: it rejects a worker with no current HR row (the AR-018 case) or with two (E-028).
2. Matrix check: a permission already in the role goes straight to provisioning.
3. Approval by the system's business owner from the asset register: A-001 Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001); A-002 Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007); A-006 and A-009 Janelle Cardinal (E-008); A-010 Tomás Rivera (E-006); A-007, A-008, A-012 and A-013 Marcus Bell (E-002). Owners may delegate in writing to named unit managers. The Pharmacy System (A-005) has no business owner, so its requests stay closed until the sponsor names one.
4. Provisioning in the Identity Directory (A-007), with the ticket number stored on the grant. Control: A-011 blocks approval when the approver is the requester or the provisioner.
5. Multifactor authentication (MFA) checked before access is released.
6. The requester confirms access works; only then does the ticket close.
7. Every grant appears in the next quarterly access review (BCN-R2-13).

## Purpose and rules

Role-based access control (RBAC): each worker has one role, the job_role in their current human resources (HR) row, and the role sets their permissions.

- Least privilege: a role holds only what everyone in it needs.
- For permissions that show health information, the Health Information Act requires the highest degree of anonymity possible and only the amount of information essential to the purpose (sections 57 and 58).
- A permission joins a role only with the approval of that system's business owner.
- Anything outside the role goes through the access request or exception process.

## Scope and rule

Segregation of duties (SoD) means no single person can complete a sensitive process alone. Kestrel rule: on the Identity Directory (A-007) no one may hold two or more of provision accounts, approve access and administer audit logs. Provisioning plus approval lets one person give anyone any access; audit-log administration lets them remove the evidence. Process rules in the same scope: nobody approves, grants or reviews their own access.

## Conflict matrix and holders

| Pair | Why it is toxic |
|---|---|
| provision accounts + approve access | Creates and authorizes access with no second person |
| provision accounts + administer audit logs | Creates access and controls the record of it |
| approve access + administer audit logs | Authorizes access and controls the record of it |

Holders on 2026-10-01 (khn_user_permissions.csv):

- provision accounts: E-009, E-017, E-033
- approve access: E-001, E-002, E-003, E-004, E-008, E-009, E-026
- administer audit logs: E-009, E-020

## Method and results

1. Filter the 171 user permission rows to A-007 and the three permissions.
2. Count distinct conflicting permissions per person; two or more is a conflict.
3. Compare granted_by with employee_id (self-grant), and reviewer_id with employee_id in khn_access_reviews.csv (self-review).

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| People holding two or more conflicting permissions | 1: E-009 holds all three |
| Self-granted permissions | 2: approve access (2025-11-03), administer audit logs (2026-02-17) |
| Self-reviews | 1: AR-001, Keep, 2026-09-12 |
| Permission rows granted by E-009 | 107 of 171 (62.6%) |

## Findings

Kevin Park (E-009) is a System Administrator. His role gives provision accounts; he also holds approve access and administer audit logs, both granted by himself. His privileged account has no multifactor authentication (MFA). He reviewed his own A-007 access (AR-001). He is also the recorded manager and the assigned reviewer of vendor engineer Raj Patel (E-015, review AR-002, overdue), whose excess Clinical Information System (A-001) view chart he granted. The design lets one account create access, approve it and erase the trail. This is a finding about control design, not about his conduct. Logged as issue I-01 in the RAID (risks, assumptions, issues, decisions) log.

## Remediation

| Action | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|
| Remove approve access and administer audit logs from E-009 | Marcus Bell (E-002) | 2026-11-04 |
| Re-approve, through Daniel Osei, every permission E-009 granted himself | Daniel Osei (E-004) | 2026-11-04 |
| Re-review AR-001 by E-004; reassign AR-002 to Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001), owner of A-001 | Programme Manager | 2026-11-16 |
| Enrol E-009 in MFA before any further privileged use | Grace Liu (E-005) | Immediately |
| Block self-approval and self-grant in A-011 and A-007 | Identity and access team | 2026-11-04 |

Approval belongs to business owners; audit-log administration belongs to security (Sam Okafor, E-020).

## Compensating controls

Three administrators (E-009, E-017, E-033) must still provision accounts. To control that power:

- Every A-007 account or group change must match an approved ticket in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011). Sam Okafor reviews the weekly match report; an unmatched change is a security incident.
- A-007 audit logs are forwarded to Sentinel SOC Services (V-04), where administrators cannot change them. This depends on the privacy review and contract safeguards under risk R-05.
- Provisioning work is shared across all three administrators.

## Residual risk and approval

An administrator could still create an account without a ticket; the weekly match would catch it within a week. Rating after controls: Low (proposed). Risk owner: Marcus Bell (E-002); Daniel Osei advises. Retest monthly by E-020, first on 2026-11-05. Target: SoD conflicts 0 on the access-governance dashboard.

Removing the conflicting permission without checking what was done with it. Re-approve every self-granted permission and review the grants the person made.
Relying on a compensating control the controlled person can switch off, such as audit logs that the same administrator manages.
Testing only system permissions and missing process conflicts such as self-review (AR-001) or a reviewer checking access they granted (AR-002).

## Decision and current state

How Kestrel confirms identity with multifactor authentication (MFA) and gives clinicians single sign-on (SSO) without slowing care at shared workstations (risk R-03). On 2026-10-01 (current identity rows):

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Enabled accounts with MFA | 17 of 40 (42.5%) |
| Clinical accounts with MFA (nurses, physicians, unit clerks, agency nurses) | 0 of 19 |
| Privileged accounts with MFA | 4 of 6 (66.7%); E-009 and E-015 not enrolled; control CT-006 Fail |

## Options considered

| Option | Assurance | Shared workstation speed | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Password only (23 accounts today) | Low | Fast | Reject |
| B. Phone app prompt at every sign-in | High | Slow; phones not always at hand | Reject for shared workstations |
| C. Badge tap plus personal identification number (PIN), then SSO inside the Virtual Desktop Service (A-008) session | Two factors: badge (have), PIN (know) | Fast | Recommend for on-site clinical work |
| D. Phishing-resistant security key (FIDO2) | Highest | Fine for occasional admin work | Recommend for privileged and vendor accounts |

## Recommendation by user group

| Group | Accounts | Method | Re-prompt (proposed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clinical staff at shared site workstations | 19 | Option C | PIN once per 12-hour shift; badge tap to unlock |
| Anyone outside Kestrel's network | All roles | Authenticator app with number matching | Every session |
| Privileged and vendor | 6, plus E-031 until confirmed | Option D | Every sign-in and elevation |
| Office staff and analysts | The rest | Authenticator app | Once per working day |

Rollout, all inside task 15: E-009 and E-015 first, then other privileged and vendor accounts, then a KGH Medicine 4A pilot of Option C, then all sites. The Release 2 pilot in task 19 (2026-11-23 to 2026-11-26) later tests the whole access service.

## Shared clinical workstations (R-03)

- A badge tap unlocks; a different badge switches user in place, so nobody works under a colleague's name.
- The screen locks after 10 minutes idle (proposed) or at the next badge tap.
- SSO carries the session to the Clinical Information System (CIS, A-001), Tracking Board (A-002), Bed Management (A-006) and dashboards (A-009) with no second password.
- Today's sign-in time on Medicine 4A is timed before the change, as the baseline. The Medicine 4A pilot then measures badge tap to open chart: no increase on the baseline (agreed with Janelle Cardinal) and a proposed target of 10 seconds or less. Janelle Cardinal decides go or no-go for the other units from the pilot data.

## Single sign-on and federation risk

The Identity Directory (A-007) is the identity provider for A-008, A-009, A-011 and A-013. Benefit: one place to disable a leaver. Risks:

- One stolen identity opens many systems: phishing-resistant MFA for privileged and vendor accounts, number matching for remote users, short sessions for cloud services, sign-in alerts to Sam Okafor (E-020).
- If A-007 fails nobody signs in: it is tier 1 with a 2-hour recovery time objective, and restore test CT-003 passed in 1.5 hours on 2026-09-10. Break-glass covers the gap.

## Break-glass access

1. Sign-in failure: one sealed CIS emergency account per site (KGH, ARH, CVH, PGH), locked away with the nursing supervisor on duty. Use alerts security at once, is reviewed the next business day, and the password is changed. Two A-007 emergency administrator accounts use security keys in a safe, retrieved by two people.
2. Record access outside a clinician's care relationship in the CIS: a reason is required, the access is logged, and Priya Raman's (E-003) privacy team reviews it.

Every emergency account is tested each quarter (proposed).

## Account recovery

- Lost badge: in person with photo ID; temporary badge for the shift.
- Lost phone or key: the service desk calls back the number in the human resources (HR) record, confirms with the manager, then issues an 8-hour temporary pass (proposed).
- Never reset MFA on an inbound call alone.
- Privileged accounts: a second administrator plus Daniel Osei's approval.

## Acceptance criteria and residual risk

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| 100% of enabled privileged accounts on MFA (agreed) | CT-006 retest |
| Pilot sign-in time meets the proposed target | Medicine 4A data, signed by E-008 |
| Break-glass works at all four sites and alerts | Acceptance tests UAT-16 |
| Unverified MFA reset refused | Acceptance test UAT-17 |

Residual risk: a badge can be lost or copied, so badge plus PIN is weaker than a security key. Accepted by Marcus Bell on Daniel Osei's advice, for on-site clinical use only. R-03 stays open with Janelle Cardinal until the pilot proves the sign-in time.
mistakes: Choosing the strongest method for everyone and ignoring clinical workflow. Nurses then share sessions or keep workstations open, which is worse than a well-designed badge and PIN.
Leaving break-glass accounts untested or unmonitored, so they fail in a real outage or become a permanent back door.
Forgetting account recovery. An attacker who can talk the service desk into an MFA reset walks straight past the MFA you just rolled out.
Treating SSO only as a convenience. The identity provider becomes a single point of failure and the most valuable target on the network.

## Elevation (just-in-time)

1. The administrator requests elevation in the privileged access management (PAM) tool, quoting an approved change or incident ticket in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011).
2. Another administrator approves; for A-007 changes, Daniel Osei's delegate. Nobody approves their own elevation.

Four vendors have remote access: Meridian Clinical Systems (V-01), NorthArc Cloud (V-02), Sentinel SOC Services (V-04) and Lumen Analytics Partners (V-05).

- Accounts stay disabled until the Kestrel sponsor raises a ticket for a session and the system's business owner approves; access ends with the session.

Privileged sign-ins, elevations and audit-setting changes are logged in A-007 and forwarded to Sentinel SOC Services, subject to the privacy review under risk R-05. Sam Okafor (E-020) is alerted to:

- an elevation with no matching ticket;
- any change to audit-log settings;
- break-glass use;
- a vendor session outside its approved window.

## Emergency use

Two A-007 break-glass administrator accounts, with security keys in a safe, retrieved by two people (Marcus Bell or Daniel Osei plus an administrator). - Quarterly: privileged access is also part of the access review (BCN-R2-13).

|---|---|---|

| Vendor or agency accounts with no end date | 1 (E-015) | 0 (proposed) |
| Vendor sessions with an approved ticket | Not recorded today | 100% (proposed) |

Letting the person who will use elevated rights approve them, or sending approvals to a shared mailbox nobody owns.

Monitoring privileged activity with logs that the administrators themselves can change or delete.

## Q3 2026 baseline

khn_access_reviews.csv on 2026-10-01:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Review items | 24: 18 due by 2026-09-30, 6 due 2026-10-15 |
| Due items completed on time | 12 of 18 (66.7%); control CT-007 Fail |
| Overdue | 6: AR-002, AR-004, AR-006, AR-012, AR-014, AR-016 |
| Decisions on valid items | Keep 11, Modify 1, Remove 2 |
| Kept under an exception | 1 (AR-010) |

Problems behind the numbers:

- AR-001: Kevin Park (E-009) reviewed his own access. It counts as completed above but is not independent.
- AR-006: completed 2026-08-28, before it was assigned on 2026-09-01, so it is not valid evidence.
- AR-018: reviews E-045, who is not in HR records. A Clinical Information System (CIS) account exists for someone HR does not know.
- AR-003: Remove decided for E-014 on 2026-09-25, yet the account was still enabled.

## Workflow steps

1. Launch on the first business day of the last month of each quarter (proposed). The campaign joins enabled Identity Directory (A-007) accounts to current HR rows: one item per person per system.
2. Assign: the reviewer is the HR manager. Where the manager is unknown (E-037 points to E-099), the system owner names one, as AR-024 did with E-022.
3. The reviewer sees role, permissions compared with the role-to-permission matrix (excess flagged), last sign-in, HR status and end date.
4. Decide Keep, Modify or Remove. Keep on an excess permission needs an exception ID (BCN-R2-14).
5. Modify and Remove open a ticket in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011), done within 5 working days (proposed) and confirmed by a second check.
6. Daniel Osei signs the campaign report; the export is kept as audit evidence.

## Rules for a valid review

- Dates are system timestamps; a completion before assignment is rejected.
- Nobody reviews their own access, and where possible not access they granted.
- Every item needs a decision; a blank is overdue.
- The person reviewed must exist in HR; if not, the account is investigated, not just removed.
- A decision counts only when its action is confirmed.

## Escalation

Timings are proposed for the first two cycles, then reviewed.

| When | Action |
|---|---|
| Day 14 | Reminder to the reviewer |
| Day 21 | Escalate to the reviewer's manager |
| Due date passed | Overdue on the access-governance dashboard; system owner and Daniel Osei told |
| 10 working days overdue | Vendor, agency and privileged access suspended; clinical staff escalated to Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001) instead, so care is not interrupted (proposed) |

## Q3 recertification actions

| Item | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| AR-001 | Independent re-review | Daniel Osei (E-004) |
| AR-002 | Reassign from E-009 to the A-001 business owner | Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001) |
| AR-003 | Disable E-014 and confirm | Grace Liu (E-005) |
| AR-004 | Remove: E-027 is a leaver | Hannah Brooks (E-021) |
| AR-006 | Repeat the review of E-028 | Tomás Rivera (E-006) |
| AR-012, AR-014, AR-016 | Escalate to the reviewers' managers: E-001 for E-022 and E-007; E-002 for E-005 | Programme Manager |
| AR-018 | Confirm the CIS account is gone; find how it was created | Nora Lindqvist (E-018) with Daniel Osei |
| AR-010 | Register the exception as EX-001 | Marcus Bell (E-002) |

## Measures and evidence

| Measure | Baseline (data) | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Due reviews completed on time | 66.7% | 100% (agreed) |
| Overdue reviews | 6 | 0 (proposed) |
| Self-reviews | 1 (AR-001) | 0 (proposed) |
| Remove decisions actioned within 5 working days | AR-003 not actioned | 100% (proposed) |

Each campaign export, with timestamps, decisions and confirmations, is kept under Kestrel's records retention schedule.

Letting a person review their own access (AR-001) or the access they granted (AR-002).

items.purpose: The access exception process handles the cases where someone needs access that the role-to-permission matrix or a security rule does not allow. It makes every exception time-bound, approved by a named risk owner, protected by compensating controls and watched until it ends. Daniel Osei (E-004) owns the process and advises on risk; the business owner of the affected system accepts the risk; the service desk records each exception and removes it when it expires. It applies from 2026-11-05 and closes the gap shown by review AR-010, which recorded an exception that nobody can trace.

sections.heading: Purpose and when an exception is allowed
sections.guidance: Define an exception and the conditions that must all be true before one is considered. Use the real gap that triggered the process. It is good when a manager can tell from this section alone whether to ask for an exception or for a change to the role.

sections.guidance: List the rules no approver can waive, such as privileged access without multifactor authentication (MFA) or approving your own access. It is good when the list matches Kestrel's security rules, including the duty-conflict rule on the Identity Directory.

| Approver | Marcus Bell (E-002), Chief Information Officer |
| Version and date | 1.0, 2026-11-05 |
| Status | Approved; in force from 2026-11-05 |

## Purpose and when an exception is allowed

An access exception lets a person hold access that the role-to-permission matrix (BCN-R2-08) or a security rule does not allow, for a limited time, because care or the business needs it. It is allowed only when all of these are true:

- the need is specific (person, system, permission) and has an end date;
- no role or request route meets it;
- compensating controls reduce the risk;
- a named risk owner accepts what remains.

Why now: review AR-010 marked Arjun Mehta's (E-039) access as kept under an exception, but no reason, approver or end date exists anywhere.

## What can never be an exception

- A privileged account without multifactor authentication (MFA).
- Approving or reviewing your own access.
- Holding two or more of provision accounts, approve access and administer audit logs on the Identity Directory (A-007).
- Access for a worker with no current human resources (HR) record, or after the worker's end date.
- Shared or generic accounts, apart from sealed break-glass accounts.

## Request and approval

1. The manager raises the request in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011): who, system, permission, reason, start and end date (90 days at most, proposed) and proposed controls.
2. Daniel Osei's security team rates the risk and checks the controls.
3. The business owner of the system approves as risk owner. Privileged exceptions also need Daniel Osei's countersignature.
4. If the access shows identifying health information beyond the role, Priya Raman (E-003) confirms it stays within the Health Information Act limits on the least amount of information and the highest degree of anonymity (sections 57 and 58).
5. The identity and access team grants the access, tagged with the exception ID.

## Compensating controls and monitoring

Typical controls: read-only instead of change rights, activity logging with a monthly review by Sam Okafor (E-020), session recording for vendors, shorter session time-outs. A weekly report lists every permission tagged with an exception ID, and the quarterly access review shows each one to its owner.

## Expiry, renewal and closure

- The permission is removed automatically on the end date.
- The risk owner is reminded 10 working days before the end (proposed).
- Renewal is a new request with fresh evidence. After two renewals (proposed) the need is treated as permanent and the role matrix is changed through change control instead.
- Closure records the removal date and who confirmed it.

## Exception register

| ID | Worker and access | Risk owner | Controls | Ends | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EX-001 | E-039 Arjun Mehta, NorthArc Cloud (V-02): standing privileged remote support to the Backup Platform (A-012); source AR-010 | Marcus Bell (E-002), A-012 business owner | MFA enrolled; session logging; account end date 2026-12-31 | When just-in-time vendor sessions go live, no later than 2026-11-30 (proposed) | Open; registered after the fact |

The 8 excess grants listed in BCN-R2-08 are not exceptions. Each is removed unless its business owner approves an exception through this process.

## Measures

| Measure | Baseline (data) | Target (proposed) |
|---|---|---|
| Review items marked exception with no register ID | 1 (AR-010) | 0 |
| Open exceptions past their end date | Not tracked before | 0 |
| Exceptions without a named risk owner | Not tracked before | 0 |
mistakes: Granting open-ended exceptions. Without an end date an exception becomes an undocumented role.
Making IT the risk owner. The business owner of the system accepts the risk; security advises.
Recording only 'exception = Y', as review AR-010 did, with no ID, reason, approver or end date, so nobody can check it later.
Using exceptions to avoid fixing the role matrix. Repeated exceptions for the same need mean the role itself is wrong.

| Title | Access-governance dashboard |
| Owner and approver | Daniel Osei (E-004), Chief Information Security Officer |
| Built by | Tomás Rivera (E-006) |
| Version and date | 1.1, 2026-11-13 (data as of 2026-10-01) |
| Status | Approved |

## Purpose and audience

One page showing whether access at Kestrel is under control, through eight measures, from missed leavers to multifactor authentication (MFA) gaps and segregation-of-duties (SoD) conflicts. Used weekly by Daniel Osei, Marcus Bell (E-002), Grace Liu (E-005), Priya Raman (E-003), Nora Lindqvist (E-018), Sam Okafor (E-020) and the identity and access team. It reports the Release 2 charter measures.

## Data and model

Import-mode semantic model; tables keep their source names:

- khn_identity: Power Query keeps each worker's current row (latest effective_from), so 43 rows become 42.
- khn_user_permissions (171 rows), khn_role_permissions (39), khn_access_reviews (24).
- FactServiceTicket with the Release 1 rules (219 rows).

khn_identity[employee_id] relates one-to-many, single direction, to khn_user_permissions and khn_access_reviews; khn_role_permissions stays unrelated. AR-018 (E-045) has no identity row and shows under (Blank) on purpose (rule DQ-10). Snapshot measures use the extract date, 2026-10-01.

## Measures (DAX)

Data Analysis Expressions (DAX), held in one measure table. Every snapshot measure uses the as-of date 2026-10-01, and + 0 shows a zero count as 0 instead of blank.

```
Accounts =
COUNTROWS ( khn_identity )

Missed Leavers =
VAR AsOf = DATE ( 2026, 10, 1 )
RETURN
    COUNTROWS (
        FILTER (
            khn_identity,
            khn_identity[account_status] = "Enabled"
                && (
                    khn_identity[hr_status] = "Terminated"
                        || (
                            NOT ISBLANK ( khn_identity[effective_to] )
                                && khn_identity[effective_to] < AsOf
                        )
                )
        )
    ) + 0

Privileged Accounts =
CALCULATE (
    [Accounts],
    khn_identity[account_status] = "Enabled",
    khn_identity[privileged] = "Yes"
)

Privileged Without MFA =
CALCULATE ( [Privileged Accounts], khn_identity[mfa_enrolled] = "No" ) + 0

Privileged MFA % =
DIVIDE ( [Privileged Accounts] - [Privileged Without MFA], [Privileged Accounts] )

Reviews Due =
VAR AsOf = DATE ( 2026, 10, 1 )
RETURN
    COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( khn_access_reviews, khn_access_reviews[due_date] < AsOf ) )

Review Completion % =
VAR AsOf = DATE ( 2026, 10, 1 )
VAR OnTime =
    COUNTROWS (
        FILTER (
            khn_access_reviews,
            khn_access_reviews[due_date] < AsOf
                && NOT ISBLANK ( khn_access_reviews[completed_date] )
                && khn_access_reviews[completed_date] >= khn_access_reviews[assigned_date]
                && khn_access_reviews[completed_date] <= khn_access_reviews[due_date]
        )
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( OnTime, [Reviews Due] )

Overdue Reviews =
VAR AsOf = DATE ( 2026, 10, 1 )
RETURN
    COUNTROWS (
        FILTER (
            khn_access_reviews,
            khn_access_reviews[due_date] < AsOf
                && (
                    ISBLANK ( khn_access_reviews[completed_date] )
                        || khn_access_reviews[completed_date] < khn_access_reviews[assigned_date]
                )
        )
    ) + 0

SoD Conflicts =
VAR PerWorker =
    ADDCOLUMNS (
        VALUES ( khn_user_permissions[employee_id] ),
        "@ConflictRights",
            CALCULATE (
                DISTINCTCOUNT ( khn_user_permissions[permission] ),
                khn_user_permissions[system_id] = "A-007",
                khn_user_permissions[permission]
                    IN { "provision accounts", "approve access", "administer audit logs" }
            )
    )
RETURN
    COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( PerWorker, [@ConflictRights] >= 2 ) ) + 0

Access Requests Within 72h % =
VAR Resolved =
    FILTER (
        FactServiceTicket,
        FactServiceTicket[TicketType] = "Access request"
            && NOT ISBLANK ( FactServiceTicket[ResolutionHours] )
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE (
        COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( Resolved, FactServiceTicket[ResolutionHours] <= 72 ) ),
        COUNTROWS ( Resolved )
    )
```

Request time also uses the Release 1 measure from the DAX catalogue (BCN-R1-20), unchanged:

```
Median Access Request Days =
DIVIDE (
    CALCULATE (
        MEDIANX (
            FILTER ( FactServiceTicket, NOT ISBLANK ( FactServiceTicket[ResolutionHours] ) ),
            FactServiceTicket[ResolutionHours]
        ),
        FactServiceTicket[TicketType] = "Access request"
    ),
    24
)
```

## Tested values

| # | Measure | Tested value (truth.json) | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Accounts by account_status | Enabled 40, Disabled 2 | None |
| 2 | Missed Leavers | 2 (E-014, E-027) | 0 (agreed) |
| 3 | Privileged Accounts | 6 | Each justified (proposed) |
| 4 | Privileged Without MFA; Privileged MFA % | 2 (E-009, E-015); 66.7% | 0; 100% (agreed) |
| 5 | Review Completion % | 66.7% (12 of 18 due) | 100% (agreed) |
| 6 | Overdue Reviews | 6 | 0 (proposed) |
| 7 | SoD Conflicts (segregation of duties) | 1 (E-009) | 0 (proposed) |
| 8 | Median Access Request Days; Access Requests Within 72h % | 4.26; 27.3% | 1; 80% (agreed) |

Method: this query in DAX query view, compared with truth.json.

```
EVALUATE
ROW (
    "Enabled", CALCULATE ( [Accounts], khn_identity[account_status] = "Enabled" ),
    "Disabled", CALCULATE ( [Accounts], khn_identity[account_status] = "Disabled" ),
    "Missed leavers", [Missed Leavers],
    "Privileged", [Privileged Accounts],
    "Privileged without MFA", [Privileged Without MFA],
    "Privileged MFA %", [Privileged MFA %],
    "Review completion %", [Review Completion %],
    "Overdue reviews", [Overdue Reviews],
    "SoD conflicts", [SoD Conflicts],
    "Median request days", [Median Access Request Days],
    "Within 72h %", [Access Requests Within 72h %]
)
```

Slice tests by worker_type: Privileged Accounts Employee 4, Vendor 2; Missed Leavers Agency 1, Employee 1.

## Page design

- Eight cards in one row, each with its target and a text status (On target or Off target), so status never depends on colour alone.
- Action table below: employee or review IDs behind each off-target card. No names, no health information.

## Security, refresh and ownership

- Sensitivity label Confidential on the model and report.
- Workspace Beacon Access Governance: Viewer for the access-governance group; Member only for Tomás Rivera and his backup Mei Tanaka (E-013). No row-level security (RLS): every viewer may see every row, and RLS would not restrict Members anyway, because it applies only to Viewers.
- Daily refresh at 06:30 (proposed) through the on-premises data gateway from 2026-11-13, after the firewall change in BCN-R2-16.
- Data alert: the Missed Leavers card is pinned to a dashboard, and Daniel Osei and Grace Liu each set an alert on that tile for any value above 0. A data alert is personal (it notifies only the person who set it) and works only on dashboard tiles that are cards, gauges or key performance indicator (KPI) visuals.
- Measure changes need Daniel Osei's approval.
mistakes: Counting rows in the raw identity file. E-028 has two rows, so Accounts shows 43 and 41 enabled instead of 40; keep one current row per worker first.
Counting AR-006 as complete because it has a completion date. It was completed before it was assigned, so it is overdue.
Using TODAY() as the as-of date, so the figures drift every day and no longer match the tested values.
Letting a blank card stand for zero. Add + 0 so Missed Leavers shows 0, not blank, once the target is reached.

## Team and purpose

Release 2 purpose: give every clinician the right access on day one and remove it on the last day, with proof, by the acceptance gate on 2026-11-26.

| Member | Release 2 role |
|---|---|
| Programme Manager | Leads the release; keeps this charter |
| Grace Liu (E-005) | Access service owner |
| Tomás Rivera (E-006) | Access-governance dashboard and its refresh |
| Kevin Park (E-009), Lucas Girard (E-033) | Directory and provisioning setup |
| Ahmed Haddad (E-017) | Network and firewall changes |
| Nora Lindqvist (E-018) | Human resources (HR) events and data |
| Sam Okafor (E-020) | Security monitoring and tests |
| Janelle Cardinal (E-008), Aisha Mahmoud (E-010) | Clinical workflow and acceptance testing |

Advisers: Daniel Osei (E-004), security; Priya Raman (E-003), privacy.

## Values and ground rules

1. Patient care comes first: no change that could affect clinical systems runs in clinical hours without approval through change control.
2. Raise a problem with the person first, then at stand-up. Never open with an email copied to executives.
3. Argue about the work, never the person.
4. Decide with evidence: Kestrel data, test results and the schedule.
5. Say early when you are blocked; asking for help is expected.

## Decision-making and escalation

- Inside one person's area: that person decides after consulting those affected.
- Across areas: aim for agreement at stand-up. With no agreement in 2 working days, the Programme Manager facilitates a session and decides if the session cannot.
- Changes to scope, schedule or cost baselines go to the change-control board chaired by Marcus Bell (E-002); priority clashes between releases go to Dr. Helen Marchetti.
- Decisions go in the RAID log (risks, assumptions, issues, decisions) the same day.

## Communication and working agreements

1. Stand-up 08:45 to 09:00 each working day.
2. Risk and issue review every Thursday.
3. Reply to team messages within 1 working day.
4. Production changes follow Kestrel change control, with no exception for programme work.
5. Testing with clinical staff is booked through their unit managers.
6. Weekly status to the sponsor through the earned value status report.
7. Added in 1.1: any network or firewall change touching clinical traffic goes on the release plan as soon as the need is known, runs in an overnight window approved through change control, and has a tested rollback.

## Conflict-resolution approach

Disagreement about the work is normal and often useful. The team deals with it early and privately first, separates positions (what each person asks for) from interests (why they need it), and uses collaborate and problem solve by default so both needs are met. Compromise is used only when both needs cannot be met, forcing only for an immediate safety or compliance risk, and nobody smooths over or walks away from a live conflict.

## Conflict record

| Field | CF-01: gateway firewall change window |
|---|---|
| Raised | 2026-11-09 at stand-up; email copied to Marcus Bell that afternoon |
| Parties | Tomás Rivera (E-006), Clinical Analytics Lead; Ahmed Haddad (E-017), Network Engineer |
| Subject | When to make the firewall change the on-premises data gateway needs to refresh the access-governance dashboard (BCN-R2-15) |
| At stake | No tested refresh before acceptance testing on 2026-11-23 and the gate on 2026-11-26 |

Positions and interests:

- Tomás wanted the change during the day on 2026-11-10. Interest: time to build and test the refresh before testing, while Lumen Analytics Partners (V-05) can still help (contract ends 2026-11-30, risk R-07) and because he alone knows the model (risk R-06).
- Ahmed refused a daytime change: the same firewall carries Virtual Desktop Service (A-008) traffic that clinicians at every site use to reach the Clinical Information System. Kestrel's standard core-firewall window is Sunday 01:00 to 05:00, and the next one with capacity was 2026-11-22, one day before testing. Interest: no risk to clinical systems and a properly approved change.

Resolution:

1. 2026-11-09: the Programme Manager met each of them privately to hear the facts and the need behind each position.
2. 2026-11-10, 10:00: facilitated session. Shared goal agreed first: a safe change and a tested refresh before testing. Options were compared on clinical risk, test time and approval: daytime change (rejected, clinical risk); 2026-11-22 window (rejected, no test time); lunchtime change (rejected, still clinical hours); an extra overnight window that week (chosen).
